newsitem.title: UK: NWE VGO prices slump as refiners prefer cheap crud.
newsitem.headline: NWE VGO prices slump as refiners prefer cheap crud.

text.p: VGO prices have slumped in Europe with plentiful supply finding difficulty attracting buyers who still prefer to refine cheap and profitable crude, traders said.
The U.S. arbitrage window was still thoroughly shut, traders said, and although there was a draw-down of U.S. VGO storage stocks it would not support prices until mid to late May.
"I think May will be better but I still don't see it as strong," said one trader, adding that European and African cargoes were still unsold and would continue to weigh on prices.
A Spanish refiner was heard to have sold a cargo of low sulphur VGO to a Swiss trader on Tuesday at a floating price described as "keen" by the market.
It came on the back of a deal from Scandinavian refiner Preem that saw a co-load of low and high sulphur go to Conoco Germany and Shell Netherlands respectively, traders said.
There was little chance of short-term improvement, traders said.
"Its definitely going to come off more," one active trader said.
